newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan one-month NCDs average yield at 5.968 pct.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan one-month NCDs average yield at 5.968 pct.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank issued T$10 billion in one-month negotiable certificates of deposit on Wednesday at an average yield of 5.968 percent, a central bank official said.
The range of the yields was between 5.900 and 6.000 percent. Demand totalled T$13.5 billion.
Wednesday's NCD issue was the highest in value since the central bank began its current round of issues on March 3. The issue was the fifth in five days.

Central bank deputy governor Hsu Chia-tung said on Monday the bank would continue to tighten liquidity in an apparent effort to cool the red-hot stock market -- despite the side effect of relatively high short-term interest rates.
Hsu said recent interest rates hikes reflected a stock market rally that as of Wednesday had seen the Taiwan share index rise 22 percent in 1997 alone.

The central bank had repeatedly issued NCDs in recent sessions in a strategy widely seen as aiming to keep a lid on the loose liquidity that many experts say has been fuelling the sizzling stock market rally.
